title: MetaDNS: Enhancing Exploration in Discrete Neural Samplers via Metadynamics
claim: Standard samplers collapse into one low-energy mode; adding a history-dependent bias drives exploration across barriers, and reweighting recovers the true multimodal distribution.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, left baseline vs two-step method, dashed arrows show bias and reweighting
description: Three side-by-side panels show a 1-D double-well energy landscape drawn as a dark-blue curve over a gray background. The left panel, under the header 'SOTA Discrete Neural Samplers', has yellow dots clustered in one deep minimum and a dotted, unexplored second well, captioned 'Mode Collapse'. The middle and right panels sit under a shared 'MetaDNS' header. In the middle panel a purple bias curve with a shaded lavender fill lifts the yellow samples with upward dashed arrows, so some samples cross the barrier and appear as red or pink crosses in the second well. A curved orange-red arrow marks barrier crossing. The caption reads 'Add Bias to Encourage Exploration'. In the right panel the faded biased curve sends the samples back down with downward arrows onto the original landscape, now populating both wells. Its caption reads 'Recover True Multi-modal Distribution'. The eye goes first to the clustered yellow dots on the left, then to the purple bias.
caption: Scheme for MetaDNS. (Left) State of the art (SOTA) discrete neural samplers suffer from mode collapse at low temperatures: samples concentrate in a single deep minimum of the multi-modal energy landscape. (Middle) MetaDNS adds a history-dependent bias potential (purple) that raises the energy in frequently visited regions, flattening the landscape and encouraging exploration across energy barriers to visit multiple minima. (Right) Samples drawn from the biased distribution are reweighted to recover the true multi-modal target distribution on the original energy landscape.
abstract: Sampling from discrete distributions with multiple modes and energy barriers is fundamental to machine learning and computational physics. Recent discrete neural samplers like MDNS suffer from mode collapse and fail to sample high-energy barrier regions between modes, which is critical for free energy estimation and understanding phase transitions. We propose Metadynamics Discrete Neural Sampler (MetaDNS), a general framework integrating well-tempered metadynamics into discrete diffusion or autoregressive samplers. By maintaining an adaptive, history-dependent bias potential along selected low-dimensional coordinates, MetaDNS forces exploration of previously inaccessible regions, enabling free energy reconstruction infeasible with standard neural samplers due to a lack of high-energy samples. On challenging low-temperature benchmarks including Ising, Potts, and the copper-gold binary alloy, MetaDNS reproduces the thermodynamic distribution. Compared to MCMC-based metadynamics, MetaDNS also achieves comparable exploration requiring fewer bias deposition steps.
